evidence.quote: Use this to list the Organization Memberships for all users belonging to an organization
This endpoint can also be used to retrieve your organization URI.
Returns a list of activity log entries
Use `client_id` for username and `client_secret` for password.

assumptions: Calendly has no per-user last-active field, so usage comes from the activity log. That endpoint needs an Enterprise plan; on other plans usage will not be available.

The source did not give OAuth authorize or token URLs, so only the Personal Access Token (bearer) method is listed. The Basic scheme is described as client_id/client_secret, which looks like it is for OAuth app token exchange, not server access.
The organization is found by first calling /users/me and reading current_organization. The token owner needs permission to list organization memberships (admin or owner).
The context step and its extracted value are both named org_uri so the {{context.org_uri}} references resolve; this binding is assumed to match how the runtime stores context values.
The source gives no user status field, so user status is left empty. Memberships returned may not include invited-but-pending or removed people.
Page size 100 and the count parameter are assumed; the maximum page size was not stated in the source.
The activity-log sort value 'occurred_at:asc' is assumed; the source lists a sort parameter without its allowed values.
Activity log actor.uri is assumed to be the same user URI as the membership user.uri; the source does not confirm this, and some actors may not be users.
Rate limits are not stated in the source and are left empty.
Activity log date-window parameters min_occurred_at and max_occurred_at are assumed to accept ISO 8601 timestamps.
